memory_update.text: Technology theme should be split into AI compute demand anchors and second-order physical/digital infrastructure chokepoints rather than analyzed as a single software/semiconductor basket.
Advanced-package substrate materials, including build-up film and copper-bonding surface chemistry, are a priority underfollowed node for AI semiconductor research.
MLCC dielectric powders, especially high-end barium titanate for AI server capacitors, are a priority underfollowed node for next-layer electronics component research.
Data-center electrical infrastructure, including transformers, switchgear, cables, conductors, and connectors, is a priority second-order beneficiary lane tied to AI infrastructure.
Specialized AI cloud capacity is a speculative_shadow lane that requires strong evidence on contracted utilization, power access, financing, and customer quality before candidate survival.

Layer 1B should build a public-company universe across US, Japan, Taiwan, Korea, Europe, and India, then tag each candidate by revenue purity, analyst attention, market cap, customer evidence, and falsification risk.

layer1a.summary: Layer 1A decomposes the broad Technology theme into chokepoint-oriented research lanes rather than obvious mega-cap AI exposure. The highest-quality starting map is: AI compute demand is pulling on advanced packaging, HBM-adjacent substrates, optical/networking, data-center power/cooling, grid interconnection, and board-level passive components. For underfollowed discovery, the strongest lanes are one or two steps below obvious winners: FC-BGA substrate materials and chemistry, MLCC dielectric powders, transformer/switchgear/cable suppliers, thermal-management and power-conditioning components, specialized AI cloud capacity, and cybersecurity/automation vendors embedded in critical infrastructure compliance workflows. This is an initial decomposition only, not a security recommendation. Later layers should verify public-company exposure, revenue purity, customer concentration, backlog, capex, capacity constraints, and valuation/pricing.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: The investable chokepoint may sit below substrate makers: substrate yield, build-up insulating film, and surface chemistry may be harder to scale or substitute than finished substrate capacity.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Prioritize sub-USD 50B and especially USD 300M-10B names where exposure is not already fully associated with AI accelerators. Include larger names only as reference anchors.
supply_chain_nodes.node: Advanced-package substrates and upstream substrate materials
supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Use substrate leaders as context but hunt for listed suppliers with FC-BGA, ABF substrate, copper-bonding chemistry, plating chemistry, surface treatment, or specialty film exposure. Confirm segment revenue, AI/HPC substrate customer exposure, capex, and customer qualification cycles.
supply_chain_nodes.underfollowed_angle: These suppliers may be covered as chemicals, materials, or electronics components rather than AI infrastructure, creating cross-sector analyst blind spots.
supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: AI accelerators and HBM-heavy packages require high-performance substrates, build-up films, and copper adhesion/surface chemistry. These are beneath the obvious GPU and HBM producers but can constrain package yield and scaling.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: High-end sub-100nm barium titanate powder for thin-layer MLCCs may be structurally tight because production requires specialized wet-chemical processes and long process learning curves.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Look for Japan, Korea, Taiwan, and specialty-chemical listings in the USD 300M-10B range; avoid treating diversified chemical groups as pure plays without segment evidence.
supply_chain_nodes.node: AI server MLCC upstream dielectric powders
supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Map MLCC makers first, then identify merchant powder suppliers and public companies with high-end BaTiO3, nano-hydrothermal, oxalate co-precipitation, or alkoxide synthesis capabilities. Verify whether AI server demand is visible in revenue, capacity, pricing, or order commentary.
supply_chain_nodes.underfollowed_angle: The market may focus on Murata, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, TDK, Taiyo Yuden, Yageo, and other capacitor makers while missing ceramic powder suppliers upstream.
supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: AI servers can require large counts of high-performance MLCCs, shifting demand upstream from capacitor assemblers to dielectric powder suppliers such as barium titanate producers.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: Long lead times, grid interconnection delays, and constrained transformer/switchgear manufacturing capacity may make electrical infrastructure a more durable bottleneck than headline cloud compute capex suggests.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Use Vertiv, Eaton, GE Vernova, and Quanta as reference leaders; hunt below them for small/mid-cap transformer, cable, switchgear, and connector suppliers with data-center or utility backlog.
supply_chain_nodes.node: Data-center electrical power delivery: transformers, switchgear, cables, conductors, connectors
supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Search across electrical equipment, EPC, grid services, conductor/cable manufacturers, connector makers, transformer oil, and industrial components. Verify backlog growth, data-center customer mix, pricing, lead times, and capacity additions.
supply_chain_nodes.underfollowed_angle: Many beneficiaries may look like boring industrials, utilities suppliers, or specialty materials businesses rather than technology companies.
supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: AI data centers are increasingly limited by power availability and grid interconnection, not only GPU supply. Transformers, switchgear, conductors, substations, and grid services can become second-order beneficiaries.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: The hidden bottleneck may be qualified components within thermal and power systems, not the branded data-center infrastructure integrator. Reliability, certification, and hyperscaler qualification can create switching costs.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Prefer niche industrial and component makers in USD 300M-10B range; treat very small liquid-cooling pure plays as speculative unless they show hard orders and credible manufacturing scale.
supply_chain_nodes.node: Thermal management and power-conditioning components for high-density AI racks
supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Map Vertiv and Eaton systems downward into suppliers of pumps, CDU components, heat exchangers, immersion/liquid-cooling fluids, power modules, busbars, sensors, and controls. Verify customer qualification, data-center revenue mix, margin expansion, and supply constraints.
search_queries: "AI data center" "liquid cooling" component supplier public company
supply_chain_nodes.underfollowed_angle: Component suppliers may be classified as industrial machinery, electronics, controls, or specialty fluids and receive little AI-specific coverage.
supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: Higher rack power density increases demand for liquid cooling, power distribution, voltage conversion, backup power, heat exchangers, pumps, sensors, and control systems.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: The scarce asset may be ready-to-use GPU cluster capacity with power, cooling, networking, and financing already secured, rather than ownership of the GPUs alone.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Include small/mid-cap cloud and data-center capacity names, but require stronger evidence than for established industrial suppliers because capex intensity and customer concentration can be severe.
supply_chain_nodes.node: Specialized AI cloud and scarce compute capacity providers
supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Screen for public companies with GPU cloud, neocloud, sovereign AI infrastructure, colocation-plus-compute, or AI cluster leasing exposure. Verify contracted capacity, utilization, customer concentration, financing terms, power access, and depreciation risk.
search_queries: "specialized AI cloud" public company GPU capacity
supply_chain_nodes.underfollowed_angle: Some companies may be covered as hosting, telecom, legacy internet, or infrastructure rather than AI cloud, but the risk of promotional or over-financed models is high.
supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: If frontier AI compute demand exceeds hyperscaler capacity or if customers need dedicated clusters, specialized AI cloud providers and data-center operators can become capacity bottleneck beneficiaries.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: The durable chokepoint may be integration and certification inside mission-critical workflows rather than generic cybersecurity demand. Vendors with regulated OT, utility, substation, cloud operations, or data-center automation deployments may have high switching costs.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Prefer USD 300M-10B software companies with vertical concentration and improving net retention; avoid broad cybersecurity platforms unless a critical-infrastructure segment is separately evidenced.
supply_chain_nodes.node: Cybersecurity and automation software embedded in critical infrastructure operations
supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Search for smaller public companies with OT cybersecurity, industrial identity, secure remote access, asset discovery, compliance automation, backup/recovery, or data-center workflow automation exposure. Verify customer evidence in utilities, hyperscalers, industrials, and regulated infrastructure.
search_queries: "operational technology cybersecurity" public company utility customers
supply_chain_nodes.underfollowed_angle: These companies may not screen as AI beneficiaries because they sell compliance, automation, monitoring, or security into infrastructure operators rather than selling chips or cloud capacity.
supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: AI data centers, utilities, grid assets, and industrial automation systems expand the attack surface and compliance burden. Vendors embedded in operational technology, identity, observability, backup, and automation workflows can be second-order beneficiaries.

theme_map.public_market_search_strategy: Run a two-lane funnel. Lane 1 uses reference leaders such as NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom, TSMC, ASML, Arista, Vertiv, Eaton, GE Vernova, and hyperscalers only to anchor the demand map and identify where capex is flowing. Lane 2 searches beneath those leaders for public small/mid-cap or niche suppliers with obscure industry labels, customer concentration, long qualification cycles, high switching costs, or exposure buried in segment notes. Prioritize companies in the USD 300M-10B market-cap range where possible; include USD 10B-30B only for unusually pure exposure and micro-caps only as speculative_shadow candidates. Do not rank stocks in Layer 1A; build testable nodes and search strings for later evidence gathering.
supply_side_constraints: Advanced packaging and FC-BGA constraints may be driven by yield, material qualification, and long customer validation cycles rather than simple wafer throughput.
HBM and accelerator substrate ecosystems have concentrated upstream suppliers, including insulating films and copper-bonding surface chemistry.
AI data centers face non-chip bottlenecks including power availability, cooling, transformer supply, switchgear, grid connection queues, and specialized data-center capacity.
High-end MLCC dielectric powder supply may be constrained by specialized wet-chemical production know-how and narrow supplier bases.
Electrical infrastructure suppliers can benefit second-order from AI demand even when they do not sell directly into chips or cloud software.
Cybersecurity and automation suppliers may be hidden beneficiaries if they sit inside regulated, hard-to-replace operational workflows.
